chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father said to me: 'O Ja'far! Dedicate to me such and such of my wealth for the lamenters to lament me for ten years at Mina, during the days of Mina.'

key_terms.أَوْقِفْ: Dedicate/Set aside (as endowment or specific allocation)
key_terms.بِمِنًى: At Mina (a location near Mecca significant for Hajj rituals)
key_terms.تَنْدُبُنِي: To lament me (performing the ritual of lamentation)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on paying women to lament the death of the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of employing professional mourners (nawadib) to publicly express grief for the Imams, a practice deeply rooted in pre-Islamic Arab culture and adopted by the Shia. It highlights the institutionalization of mourning rituals, specifically linking the commemoration of the Imams' deaths to the sacred time and place of Mina during Hajj, thereby integrating personal piety with communal ritual. This narration serves as a foundational juristic proof (hujjah) for the legitimacy of organized lamentation ceremonies (majalis) in Shia tradition.
